construct.constructDefinition: Teaching and Learning: self-reported digital teaching engagement/practice in the published higher-education survey. Area raw sum, not observed competence or teaching quality.

population.populationNotes: Adults teaching in higher/further education. Source study: health-sciences faculty; this separated area has no independently established administration validation. Not a school/student or validated Chinese version.

administration.timeFrame: Current practice; long-term professional goals (no fixed retrospective day window).
layoutConstraints: Keep source order and all five item-specific options. Score options in printed ascending order 0,1,2,3,4.
Prefer all six areas in original 22-item order; separated-area validity is not established.
Complete-case raw sum only. Any missing/invalid answer yields no area score; no imputation. This missingness policy is a project choice.
Do not derive global A1–C2 levels from an area or from this combination; no cross-tool total.
Estimated time is a project estimate.

intendedUses.notes: Developmental reflection on self-reported practice; area separation not independently validated.
Source study concerns higher-education health-sciences faculty, not K12 or an objectively measured performance test.

options.label: I do not or only rarely use technology in class
I make basic use of available equipment, e.g. digital whiteboards or projectors
I use a variety of digital strategies in my teaching
I use digital tools to systematically enhance teaching
I use digital tools to implement innovative pedagogic strategies
I do not use digital environments with my students
I do not monitor student activity in the online environments we use
I occasionally check on them and their discussions
I regularly monitor and analyse my students' online activity
I regularly intervene with motivating or corrective comments
My students do not work in groups
It is not possible for me to integrate digital technologies into group work
I encourage students working in groups to search for information online or to present their results in digital format
I require students working in teams to use the internet to find information and present their results in a digital format
My students exchange evidence and jointly create knowledge in a collaborative online space
Not possible in my work environment
My students do reflect on their learning, but not with digital technologies
Sometimes I use, for example, quizzes for self-assessment
I use a variety of digital tools to allow learners to plan, document or reflect on their learning
I systematically integrate different digital tools to allow learners to plan, monitor and reflect on their progress

items.content: I carefully consider how, when and why to use digital technologies in teaching, to ensure that they are used with added value
I monitor my students' activities and interactions in the collaborative online environments we use
When my students work in groups or teams, they use digital technologies to acquire and document evidence

I use digital technologies to allow students to plan, document and monitor their learning themselves E.g. quizzes for self-assessment, ePortfolios for documentation and showcasing, online diaries/blogs for reflection...

scores.label: Teaching and Learning (area raw sum)
scores.description: 4 item-specific 0–4 responses summed without reversing; range 0–16. Descriptive self-report, not a validated standalone proficiency grade.

interpretations.headline: Teaching and Learning: reflect on your current practice
interpretations.summary: These answers describe your own perception of practice in teaching and learning. A higher raw sum means you selected options describing more digital engagement; it does not establish observed competence, student outcomes or teaching quality. Consider which practices worked for your learners and which depended on time, access or institutional support. Fewer opportunities to use technology do not make you a less capable teacher. There is no norm-based high/low category here.

guidance.text: Choose one learning goal, then try one digital activity only where it adds value; review a student work sample.
If access, workload or support is limiting your options, record one specific need and discuss a feasible next step with an appropriate colleague or support team.

limitations: Higher-education English survey published by Ersoy et al. (2024), dated 2023-06-02; this is not the original school Check-In, SELFIEforTEACHERS32 or a validated Chinese edition.
Area separation and this complete-case missingness policy are project adaptations. Prefer the full original 22-item sequence; no standalone area validation or norm is claimed.
Self-report is affected by opportunities, resources and interpretation. Do not use for diagnosis, performance ranking, teacher accountability or unsupported comparisons.
report.disclaimer: Teacher developmental reflection only. Missing/invalid answers mean insufficient evidence for an area score; do not substitute zero. Background and A1–C2 self-positioning forms have no calculated scores. Results remain subject to existing recipient and publication permissions.

instruction.text: Please consider where you stand in view of the following long-term goals. The answer options are organised by increasing level of engagement. Please choose the option that best reflects your current practice. This is the Teaching and Learning area of the published higher-education survey. Each item has its own five options; keep their order. All area items are needed for a descriptive raw sum. Prefer the full 22-item sequence. This is developmental self-reflection, not an observed competence test.
